files.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: production 16-frame painted animation sprite atlas for a primary-school educational webgame.
OUTPUT GEOMETRY IS CRITICAL: one single image, EXACTLY FOUR COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS of equal rectangular animation frames, sixteen frames total. Overall image aspect ratio 4:3, preferably 3072x2304, otherwise 2048x1536. Each of the 16 cell frames is itself exactly 4:3. Every scene extends to its cell edges. Zero gutters, zero dividing lines, zero borders. No text, lettering, numbers, arrows, labels, panels, insets, title or watermark anywhere.
Read animation in row-major order: top row frames 1,2,3,4; second row 5,6,7,8; third row 9,10,11,12; bottom row 13,14,15,16. Numbers below are instructions only and must never appear in the image.
Input image role: supplied image is a visual STYLE, CHARACTER, ENVIRONMENT and BEFORE/AFTER reference; it contains TWO source views. Do NOT copy its two-column layout. Expand the action into sixteen equal frames.
Style: warm, polished primary textbook gouache illustration, soft paper pigment, sunny colors, charming East Asian boy age seven with black hair, normal stable anatomy, exactly two arms and two legs and natural five-fingered hands, same clothes as respective reference. Match supplied environment.
TEMPORAL INVARIANTS: same fixed camera and identical background registration, perspective, character head size, body size, clothing, face and object dimensions in every cell. No pan, zoom, reframing or mirroring. All sixteen frames depict sixteen DISTINCT successive moments of ONE continuous forward action, fourteen unique intermediate poses between source before and source after outcome. No duplicated endpoints or tiles. Motion readable without text.
Scene: bathroom reference. Boy stands LEFT of white sink, blue T-shirt, navy shorts, white socks and pale blue slippers. Chrome single-lever tap fixed on sink center-right, wood cabinet below, cream bathroom, mirror above, aqua soap right of tap, aqua towel far right, window and potted plant left. Sink, chrome tap BASE and SPOUT rigid and registered.
Action: right hand operates tap LEVER, then releases and gradually returns toward his body. Water responds immediately. Lever rotates upwards around actual valve pivot; spout NEVER moves. Water falls DOWN into basin by gravity.
Sixteen DISTINCT timeline instants:
1 source BEFORE: fingertips touching low closed lever, dry basin, no water.
2 fingers visibly lift lever; earliest tiny bead under outlet.
3 lever open; short first water jet begins from outlet; hand starts releasing.
4 first jet grows DOWNWARD; hand separates a little.
5 jet reaches basin, first small splash; hand retreats.
6 falling droplets advance, splash changes; elbow bends more.
7 continuous narrow stream, new droplet positions; hand comes back.
8 sustained stream, hand halfway back, arm angle visibly changed.
9 hand farther toward torso, droplets fall and splash moves.
10 relaxed forearm lower and closer to body; flow continues.
11 elbow bends differently, hand further back, new splash.
12 hand lowers near waist, new falling droplets.
13 arm relaxes toward side; water flows down.
14 hand lower again; distinct stream and splash detail.
15 hand almost resting near side; water falling.
16 source AFTER OUTCOME: tap open, healthy downward water stream splashes into basin, boy smiling and arm relaxed after withdrawing.
Fourteen genuinely progressive arm poses, lever moves first, advancing downward droplets make each cell distinct. Do not switch water off late or freeze hand on lever.

qaGrid4x4.observation: Dry basin; fingertip rests on closed lever.
Fingertips lift lever; first outlet bead.
Short downward jet appears; cause and response visible.
Jet lengthens downward; raised lever and releasing hand.
Water reaches basin; initial small splash.
Hand separates from lever; falling stream continues.
Bent forearm retreats; stream and splash active.
Hand moves further toward torso; new splash shape.
Forearm lower and closer; downward water.
Hand lowers toward waist; stream/splash changes.
Arm relaxes farther; splash continues.
Hand near side; water falls into basin.
Arm settles; open tap and distinct splash.
Stable resting pose; stream/droplet detail changes.
Stable resting pose; stream/splash detail changes.
After outcome: arm relaxed and water flowing.

limitations: Arm settles to almost identical final resting poses; stream/splash details continue changing across the late frames.

files.prompt:
Create ONE new animation sprite sheet, using the provided two-view schoolboy picture ONLY as a style/character reference.
Absolute layout: 4 EQUAL COLUMNS × 4 EQUAL ROWS = 16 frames. Entire sheet aspect 4:3, each equal frame 4:3. All frames fit fully inside the sheet, no cropped last column. Prefer 2048×1536. NO GUTTERS, BORDERS, frame lines, numbers, labels or text.
Warm sunny primary textbook gouache; same black-haired seven-year-old East Asian schoolboy as reference, white short-sleeve shirt, navy shorts, white socks, dark shoes, blue backpack.
Each frame repeats exactly the SAME fixed corridor, same fixed camera, same boy size and foot placement, same right-hand-hinged teal door. Three hinges and RIGHT jamb stay FIXED at 86% of each cell width. Single door leaf swings away into classroom; its LEFT free edge moves progressively RIGHT, revealing more classroom at left. The boy is at left of door. His right palm continuously presses ONE silver pushplate on the moving left door edge. He has exactly TWO ARMS in all frames: ONE left arm hanging down, ONE right arm pushing. ONE right hand touching the door. No extra limbs or hands. His right elbow smoothly extends as door opens. No detached forearms.
16 different moments, in row-major order, never repeat an endpoint:
row 1: closed door; open 4°; open 8°; open 12°.
row 2: open 16°; open 20°; open 24°; open 28°.
row 3: open 32°; open 36°; open 40°; open 44°.
row 4: open 48°; open 52°; open 56°; open 60°.
Thus all 14 middle poses must be visibly distinct, increasing door opening throughout the final row too. Door rotates on its actual FIXED RIGHT hinges, not sliding. Single door, single boy per cell. Camera, boy face and body SCALE, left plant/window, right bulletin board and doorframe positions are identical in every frame. Only door angle, pushing right-arm pose and opening gap change. At frame1 door is completely closed; at frame16 door is clearly open into classroom, with desks visible. Correct biomechanics and believable perspective. No double doors, phantom hands, moving hinge, mirroring or zoom.

qaGrid4x4.observation: Closed door, one pushing right palm and resting left arm; initial right-jamb registration is ~18 px right of later frames.
Small initial opening; pushing palm remains on plate; hinge settles at later-frame position.
Slightly increased opening, same boy scale and two natural arms.
Door face narrows a little further; pushing hand follows plate.
Door continues opening; no phantom hand or doubled door.
Subtle additional opening with continuous palm contact.
First clearer slit into classroom; right hinge on same jamb.
Classroom opening widens; right arm extends.
Visible classroom gap; single leaf rotates on right edge.
Larger gap and more extended pushing forearm.
Door narrows in perspective; desks increasingly visible.
Door opens farther and hand moves with pushplate.
Classroom gap wider; boy stays same scale.
More extended arm; single open door and desks behind.
Door continues opening; palm remains attached to plate.
Open-door outcome; most classroom visible and fully extended pushing arm.

limitations: Right jamb/hinge registration shifts approximately 18px between the closed first frame and the second frame; subsequent right hinge positions are stable. Early angle progression is subtle.

Scene: sunny pond reference. Boy on grassy LEFT bank, trees top-left, horizontal wooden fence behind, stones and grass along far bank, blue-green water right, few lily pads lower-right. Boy wears blue T-shirt, navy shorts, white socks and blue sneakers, stable head and body size. Small red-and-white toy cabin boat in RIGHT water; its BOW points LEFT toward boy. Same boat dimensions, red hull, white cabin, blue windows, red chimney, red flag. Far end/STERN at right. Never mirror or reverse boat.
Action and mechanics: boy pulls a golden rope with BOTH hands, making boat come toward him and toward LEFT shore. The taut straight loaded rope is visibly connected continuously from BOTH gripping hands to metal bow eye on LEFT boat tip. No broken rope, detached end, slack loaded span or passing through hull. Loose rope tail may hang below hands, separate from taut span.
FIXED CAMERA; fixed bank and boy foot positions. Boat translates monotonically LEFT in screen coordinates, toward boy, by small equal steps. It does NOT move right, get larger or farther offshore. Wake stays BEHIND stern to RIGHT, changing each cell as boat approaches. Hands pull progressively closer to torso while boy progressively bends knees and leans back slightly for effort. Natural hands, no extra limbs.
16 distinct timeline positions for boat bow, as percentage of EACH CELL width:
frame1 72% (source BEFORE; arms extended and rope taut);
frame2 70.5% (hands pull, boat immediately responds left);
frame3 69%; frame4 67.5%; frame5 66%; frame6 64.5%;
frame7 63%; frame8 61.5%; frame9 60%; frame10 58.5%;
frame11 57%; frame12 55.5%; frame13 54%; frame14 52.5%;
frame15 51%; frame16 49.5% (source AFTER, boat close to left shore).
Boy hands x position smoothly decreases from about 29% to 26% while feet stay planted, knees flex and torso leans progressively back; rope shortens loaded span but ALWAYS connects hand grips and bow eye. 14 unique progressive natural pull poses and 14 distinct intermediate boat positions. Wake behind at right, ripple sequence distinct. No repeated endpoints.

qaGrid4x4.observation: Arms extended; taut rope reaches left-facing bow, boat offshore.
Hands begin pull; boat advances left and wake begins right.
Knees flex; boat moves left, taut rope connected.
Boy leans back; boat progresses left; wake behind stern.
Pull pose deepens; shorter loaded rope and nearer boat.
Hands draw closer; bow moves left; wake behind right.
Pull continues; boat and ripples advance.
Taut hand-to-bow rope; boat continues toward left bank.
Knees bent; boat approaches bank leftwards.
Rope span shortens; boat approaches steadily.
Bow nearer hands; consistent left-facing hull.
Continued leftward travel and rear wake.
Boat near grassy shore; boy remains on bank.
Short taut rope; boat advances further left.
Boy leans back with secure grip; near-shore bow.
After outcome: boat closest to shore, taut rope and rightward trailing wake.

limitations: Motion increments are painterly rather than mathematically equal; no reversed travel was observed.
